name: Neo4j
verdict: No third-party OAuth: each customer creates Aura API client credentials (client ID and secret) in their Aura Account Settings and pastes them in. You exchange them for short-lived tokens; about 1-3 days.
needGuide: No — just collect each customer's Aura client ID and secret, ideally from a least-privileged user.

auth.detail: No user-facing OAuth for third parties. The Aura API uses OAuth 2.0 client credentials: POST https://api.neo4j.io/oauth/token with Basic auth (client ID/secret) and grant_type=client_credentials returns a 1-hour bearer token (403 once expired). Credentials are tied to the creating user, inherit that user's roles, and never expire until deleted. Database access itself is a separate Bolt URI with database credentials (per Aura convention, not re-verified here).

effort.timeToProduction: 1-3 days (build credential intake and token caching)

approval.gate: None: each customer creates their own Aura API credentials; there is no developer-registered app, review or partner program for Aura OAuth.

scopes.why: No scopes: the token inherits its creator's roles.
scopes.summary: No scopes: the token inherits the creating user's capabilities and roles. Billing endpoints are limited to 10 requests/day per organization.

cost: Free to create credentials on all tiers; API rate limits: 25 req/min on Free/Pro trial, 125 req/min on paid tiers, billing endpoints 10 req/day per organization.
prerequisites: Account and owner: No developer app needed. Your team only needs a test Aura account to build against.
Where you register: Aura console → profile menu (top right) → Account Settings → Client credentials → Aura API → Create client credential
Cost: Free to create credentials on all tiers; API rate limits: 25 req/min on Free/Pro trial, 125 req/min on paid tiers, billing endpoints 10 req/day per organization.

registerAt.path: Aura console → profile menu (top right) → Account Settings → Client credentials → Aura API → Create client credential

steps.do: Tell the customer to open Aura console → Account Settings → Client credentials → Aura API → Create client credential
Customer copies the Client ID and Client Secret (shown once) into your app's connection form
Store the secret encrypted; request a token with POST api.neo4j.io/oauth/token and cache it for under one hour
Validate with GET /v1/instances and show a clear error on 403 (expired) or revoked credentials
For data access, separately collect the Bolt URI, database user and password and keep them in the vault
Throttle to the documented rate limits and test with a free-tier account

roles.team: No developer app needed. Your team only needs a test Aura account to build against.
roles.customer: A customer user creates client credentials in their Aura Account Settings; the credentials carry that user's roles, so ask for a dedicated least-privileged user (likely) rather than an org admin. Exact org/project roles required are not documented.

testing: Use a free Aura account and a free instance: create client credentials, fetch a token, call GET https://api.neo4j.io/v1/instances.

blockers.fix: Ask customers to create them from a least-privileged user.

blockers.problem: Token expires after 1 hour with no refresh
Aura API credentials do not give database query access

automation.agentCan: Write the credential intake form, token exchange and caching code, validate with test calls, and draft the customer instructions.
automation.humanMust: The customer must log in and create the credentials; your team must handle secure secret storage sign-off.

uncertain: Which Aura roles can create credentials, whether the Aura API is available on every tier, and DB-level SSO/OIDC options were not confirmed (fetch limit reached).
Neo4j has no announced third-party OAuth.
